```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`RSYC_models` contains all published RSYC yield curves from model release
`v20260923`. It has 27,208 rows and 42 columns; each row describes one curve
for a forest measure, species, area, and source. The release was built from
upstream Git commit `c799aba24b5d99a6a7953a4dcab1dd73b0925c2c`.

```{r}
library(RSYC)
head(RSYC_models[c(
  "model_id", "response", "response_units", "strata_level", "strata_id",
  "ecozone_id", "ecoprovince_id", "ecoregion_id", "ecodistrict_id",
  "scale", "species", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4"
)])
```

The `response` column describes the forest measure: `agb` is aboveground
biomass in Mg/ha, and `volume` is total volume in m3/ha. Areas can be tiles,
ecozones, ecoprovinces, ecoregions, or ecodistricts. The table includes curves
fitted across Canada and curves fitted within individual regions. The package
functions currently use only the Canada-wide curves.

The four raw hierarchy identifier fields retain upstream codes for ecological
areas. `ecozone_id`, `ecoregion_id`, and `ecodistrict_id` are integers;
`ecoprovince_id` is character so codes such as `"10.1"` retain their source
representation. These fields provide data provenance in this release.
Ecological model selection continues to use `strata_id`, either as an
unambiguous short name or a full hierarchical path.

For ecological areas, `strata_id` gives the full sequence of names from the
ecozone down to the selected level, separated by `/`. `predict_rsyc()` also
accepts the shorter `strata_name` when that name occurs only once for the
chosen forest measure, species, and ecological level:

```{r}
rsyc_strata(
  response = "agb",
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  strata_level = "ecoregion"
)
```

Use `available_rsyc_models()` to see which curves are available without viewing
all of the fields used to fit and check the curves:

```{r}
available_rsyc_models(
  response = "volume",
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  strata_level = "tile"
)
```

`RSYC_models` also contains measures of uncertainty and variation.
`local_b1_var` and `residual_var` support local calibration with
`calibrate_rsyc()`; `predict_rsyc()` itself applies the published coefficients
without local adjustment. Because the `v20260923` coefficients differ from the
previous model release, rendered predictions and calibration examples have
been regenerated for this catalogue.
